To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the current model diet used by JECFA is a reasonable approach for assessing the dietary intake of residues of veterinary drugs.
(1) the current model diet is a valid approach to assess the chronic exposure to residues of veterinary drugs and that (2) the current model is not valid to assess acute exposure.
the current JECFA model diet is a useful tool that can be used to assess dietary exposure to residues of veterinary drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

 the development of an exposure assessment model that can be used to estimate the dietary exposure of consumers to veterinary drug residues;  the development and validation of an exposure assessment tool that can be applied by regulatory authorities and food industry for the estimation of consumer exposure to veterinary drug residues in animal-derived foods;  the evaluation of the impact of the exposure assessment model and tool on the risk management decisions of the regulatory authorities and the food industry.

the model diet approach used by JECFA is appropriate and that the model diet is not in need of revision.

the Committee is of the opinion that the following approaches are appropriate to estimate the dietary intake of residues of veterinary drugs:  The current model diet (market basket approach) should be retained as a default approach to estimate chronic dietary exposure.  For the purpose of estimating acute exposure, the current model diet can be simplified to a single food category (e.g. meat).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

 a simplified model diet was developed;  the simplified model diet was used to develop a regional model diet for the Americas;  a model diet for the European Union was developed;  a model diet was developed for the Middle East;  approaches for acute and short term dietary exposure assessment were developed; and  a model for the calculation of the margin of exposure was developed.

 The current approach for chronic dietary exposure assessment for veterinary drug residues is considered to be adequate.  The current model diet (market basket) is considered to be an acceptable and useful tool for chronic dietary exposure assessments.  The model diet is not considered to be an appropriate tool for acute dietary exposure assessments and should not be used for this purpose.  There is a need for further refinement of acute and sub-acute dietary exposure assessments for veterinary drugs.  The use of
the expert consultation has been successful in achieving its objectives and has made significant progress in addressing the issues identified by the CCRVDF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have a good understanding of the exposure assessment for chronic dietary risk assessments.
the market basket diet is a reasonable approach to use in the context of a risk assessment.
the current model diet used by JECFA is appropriate for the purposes of the JECFA decision tree approach, and that it should be retained.
